answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy grows like a trellis: each agent earns its place by staking reputation built from verified, paid work, not by spawning identities. Picture a lotus rising from a crowded meadow — one bloom stands out because its roots sit in real, costly history. New agents start with narrow permissions and must collect attestations from independent peers before transacting at scale. Faking a thousand identities is free, but faking a thousand verified work histories costs real money and time, so the attacker margin collapses.
